title: INCOSE Requirements Review Feedback (v2)
description: Reviewer decisions on AI-flagged INCOSE criterion violations, shaped so that generalizable rules can be mined across sessions, reviewers and model versions.

format_version.description: Bump on any breaking change so old exports stay parseable.

session.description: Provenance. Without this you cannot tell whether a pattern belongs to the criterion, the model, the document, or the reviewer.

analyzer.description: Which model produced the findings. Required to compare model versions rather than confounding them.

criteria_set.description: Version of the criteria definitions used (e.g. incose-gwr-4.0). Rates are not comparable across versions.

reviewer.description: Anonymous but stable id, so per-reviewer bias can be separated from consensus.

domain_expertise.description: Free text, e.g. 'avionics cyber'. Lets you check whether disagreement tracks domain.

source_document.description: Which document these requirements came from. A pattern seen in only one document is not yet generalizable.

derived_statistics.description: Convenience aggregates. Always recomputable from `requirements` — treat as cache, never as source of truth.

category.description: Parenthesised label from the source document, e.g. 'Mission Computer Secure Boot'.

edits.description: Structured, non-overlapping replacements ordered by start offset. Applying them left-to-right to original_text MUST yield final_text. This replaces the v1 splice-by-substring approach, which silently produced duplicated clauses and dropped accepted fixes.

final_text.description: The agreed requirement after applying `edits`. Validate against edits before using as a training target.

decision.description: One reviewer judgement about one flagged criterion.

finding.description: What the model asserted. Stored verbatim so the reviewer's judgement can be re-scored later against a different model's output.

affected_span.description: [start, end) character offsets into original_text. Removes the ambiguity of matching by substring when a phrase repeats.

suggestion_scope.description: Whether the suggestion replaces just the affected span or rewrites the entire requirement. Mixing the two without labelling them is what corrupted v1 final_text.

judgement.description: The two questions kept deliberately separate. Collapsing them (as v1 did) makes a low acceptance rate uninterpretable: you cannot tell whether the criterion over-detects or whether its fixes are simply poor.

violation_agreed.description: Q1 — DETECTION quality. Is this genuinely a violation? false = model false positive.

fix_action.description: Q2 — GENERATION quality. Use 'not_applicable' when violation_agreed is false.

reject_reason.description: Required when fix_action is 'reject'. 'boilerplate_non_fix' captures the dominant v1 pattern: appending 'as specified in [stakeholder need reference]', which defers the problem rather than fixing it.

user_text.description: Required when fix_action is 'modify'. This is the only field carrying reviewer-authored wording, and therefore the highest-value signal in the file.

confidence.description: Reviewer certainty. Lets low-confidence judgements be down-weighted rather than treated as ground truth.

tags.description: Optional reviewer-supplied labels for recurring patterns, e.g. 'placeholder-deferral'.

time_to_decide_ms.description: Rough proxy for difficulty. Fast rejects tend to indicate an obviously bad suggestion.

source.description: Whether the accepted wording came from the model or the reviewer.
